package_info.package_name: UI Automation Attack Tool (generic, PoC or custom malware)
package_info.package_versions: All Windows versions since XP (no package version, but all OS versions affected)
package_info.why_malicious: The tool abuses the legitimate UI Automation framework to stealthily monitor, manipulate, and exfiltrate sensitive user data from other applications, bypassing EDR detection. It leverages elevated UI interaction permissions to harvest credentials, credit card data, and perform unauthorized actions in user sessions.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user launches the malicious program)
required_permissions: read/write to other process UI elements

malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (or any language supporting COM/Win32 API)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code initializes the UI Automation COM object and registers an event handler to monitor UI element changes in other applications, enabling surveillance of sensitive user actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate programs rarely need to monitor arbitrary UI events in other processes, especially outside accessibility tools.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not create global UI Automation handlers unless for accessibility; malware does so to spy on user activity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Screen readers or accessibility tools for users with disabilities.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon UI event, e.g., user enters data in browser or chat app)
execution_context.file_location: event handler callback in malicious binary
required_permissions: read access to UI element properties

malicious_snippets.code_language: C++/C#/Python (pseudo-code, but matches UI Automation API usage)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a monitored UI element changes (e.g., credit card field), the handler reads the new value and sends it to an external server, enabling credential or financial data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reading sensitive UI fields and exfiltrating their contents is a hallmark of spyware and credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Accessibility tools should not exfiltrate or log sensitive data; this is clear abuse.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Accessibility tools may read field values for speech output, but never transmit them externally.
key_indicators: get_CurrentName() or get_CurrentValue() on sensitive fields
network exfiltration of UI element data

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after finding target UI element, e.g., browser or chat app)
execution_context.file_location: malicious binary, after traversing element tree

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After locating a target UI element (e.g., chat input), the code programmatically writes data to it, enabling message injection or command execution in user applications.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Programmatic manipulation of other applications' UI elements is rarely legitimate and is a common technique for automation-based attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not inject messages or commands into other apps without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated testing tools or accessibility input aids.
key_indicators: setValue or similar write operations on external app UI elements
targeting chat or browser input fields

attack_chain.action: Initialize UI Automation object and register event handlers to monitor UI changes in other applications.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to observe sensitive user actions in real time.

attack_chain.action: Filter UI events to identify when sensitive data (e.g., credit card info, chat messages) is entered.
attack_chain.leads_to: Harvesting of sensitive data from user sessions.

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrate harvested data to attacker-controlled server or inject malicious input into target applications.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data theft, account compromise, or further attack propagation.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual use of UIAutomationCore.dll by non-accessibility applications
Processes registering global UI Automation event handlers
Accessing or modifying UI elements in other processes
Network activity following sensitive UI events
file_indicators: Presence of binaries/scripts importing or dynamically loading UIAutomationCore.dll
Unexpected creation of UI Automation named pipes
network_indicators: Outbound connections immediately after sensitive UI activity (e.g., credit card entry)
Exfiltration to attacker-controlled domains or IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for non-accessibility processes loading UIAutomationCore.dll and registering event handlers. Flag processes that access or modify UI elements in other applications, especially if followed by network activity. Watch for creation of unexpected UI Automation named pipes. Correlate UI event monitoring with outbound network connections to detect exfiltration attempts.
